title: U.S. House · Illinois's 2nd District
area: Parts of Chicago's South Side, south suburban Cook County, and Will County

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Robin Kelly (D) ran for U.S. Senate instead of seeking re-election to this seat and did not appear on the District 2 primary ballot. Donna Miller, a Cook County Board Commissioner, won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary over ten other candidates. Mike Noack won the Republican primary.
Ashley Banks is running as a write-in independent candidate.

summary.text: Miller has served on the Cook County Board of Commissioners (6th District) since December 2018, after a career in healthcare consulting, sales training and marketing and leadership roles at Planned Parenthood of Illinois and Illinois Democratic Women. She won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary for the open seat, and her campaign website says she is running to lower costs for working families and expand access to healthcare.

background.text: Born September 7, 1965 (as Donna Lynne Black), according to Wikipedia, and spent most of her youth in Chicago; graduated from Lane Technical High School in 1983. Describes herself as "an original Chicago girl" whose family has lived in Cook County for more than 120 years.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Howard University (1987, per Wikipedia) and took graduate business courses at Pepperdine University in 1992. Sources differ on the field of her bachelor's degree, so it is not stated here.

Worked in healthcare consulting and as a professional trainer: Ballotpedia lists sales training with Genentech and UnitedHealth Group and marketing with the American Heart Association, and says she worked as an independent sales-training and marketing consultant for 15 years.

According to her campaign website, she has also had an internship on Capitol Hill, volunteered with the Red Cross, and served as Board Chair of Planned Parenthood of Illinois, Vice-President of Illinois Democratic Women and President of Democratic Women of the South Suburbs.
Ran for the Democratic nomination for the 15th District Illinois State Senate seat in 2012 and finished second to Napoleon Harris, according to Wikipedia.

Won the Democratic primary for Cook County Board of Commissioners, 6th District, on March 20, 2018 and the November 6, 2018 general election, taking office December 3, 2018; she was re-elected on November 8, 2022 and is not seeking re-election to the county board in 2026.

On the Cook County Board she chairs the Asset Management, Contract Compliance and Veterans committees and is vice-chair of Workforce, Housing and Community Development. Her campaign website says she has led initiatives in health equity, veteran services and economic development.

Won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary for Illinois' 2nd District with 40.4% of the vote (34,034 votes) in a field of 10 candidates; the seat is open because U.S. Rep. Robin Kelly is running for U.S. Senate.
According to her campaign website, she is married to Dr. David E. Miller, has two sons, and is a member of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Inc.

priorities.text: Says she has "spent her career serving the community and fighting to lower costs for working families, increase opportunity, and expand access to healthcare, particularly for women and communities of color."
Cites family legacy in public service, saying her great-grandfather was a Pullman Porter and her grandmother, mother, and sister were all teachers.
Says she is running "to fight back against those in Washington who are trying to tear down all of the progress she's made for working families" and to "build a future we can all afford."

summary.text: Noack is a truck driver from Bonfield, Illinois, and the Republican nominee for the open 2nd District seat. On his campaign website he describes himself as "a trucker, not a politician" and lists healthcare costs, energy and fiscal responsibility among his issues.

background.text: Born in Bonfield, Illinois, according to Ballotpedia; says on his campaign website that he has lived in Kankakee County for 32 years.
Works as a truck driver; his campaign website says he holds a commercial driver's license (CDL) and has driven on highways in the district and across the country.
Says his wife is from Japan, which he cites as the reason legal immigration is a personal issue for him.
Was the only Republican in the March 17, 2026 primary for the open seat and advanced to the November general election.

candidates.name: Ashley Banks
candidates.ballotNote: Running as a write-in independent candidate

summary.text: Banks is a Chicago-area freelance journalist, photographer and election judge running as an independent write-in candidate. In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey she describes her campaign, "Banks for IL-02," as focused on respect, value and transparency in government.

background.text: Born in Chicago; says in her Ballotpedia survey that she is 40 years old and was born and raised in Illinois.

Graduated from Crete-Monee High School. By her own account she is completing a journalism degree at Olive-Harvey College and an international marketing degree at DePaul University, and attended Central Arizona College for teaching.
Says she has worked as a tutor for DePaul University, a CTA bus driver, a truck driver and an Amazon warehouse employee.

Describes herself as a freelance journalist, photographer and election judge who has been involved in politics and community work since her teenage years; Ballotpedia lists her profession as entrepreneur.
Declared as a write-in independent candidate for the November 3, 2026 general election.

priorities.text: Says her experience living and working in the district gives her real experience representing it, summed up in her campaign's own phrase: "Real Experience. Real Representation."
Campaign focuses on "restoring respect, value, and transparency between the people and those elected to serve them."
Says she stands for "efficiency, timely action, and clear plans that keep District 2 moving forward."

researchNotes: No Candidate Connection survey was found for Mike Noack, and his Ballotpedia profile lists only birthplace and profession; his campaign website (noack4congress.com) was found and gives his biography, but no education, prior offices or employer history. Miller's biography draws on her campaign website, the Cook County page, Ballotpedia and Wikipedia (Ballotpedia and Wikipedia differ on the field of her Howard University degree). Banks's material comes from her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no education beyond high school could be confirmed as completed.
